comments.author: m0rphling
comments.story: Goldman Sachs is spending $100M to shave milliseconds off stock trades
comments.why: Explains IEX using fiber coil to add fairness delay
comments.text: Tom Scott did a nice video [1] on IEX's setup with 38 miles of fiber to add enough latency as a mechanism of fairness. Purportedly, this benefits all exchanges after it was successfully deployed. It seems like the incentives are not there for larger, more established exchanges to implement such blanket latency. So, firms like GS see a benefit to this kind of investment. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: kmeisthax
comments.story: Commercial Interests Petition FCC for High Power Allocation on Shortwave
comments.why: Shows exchange delaying trades with a box of fiber
comments.text: There's actually an exchange that did this. In order to avoid software problems that would negate the slowing, they actually plugged their servers into a giant box full of fiber optic cable. If someone manages to get past that, then they don't have an HFT firm, they have a time machine. [VIDEO]

comments.author: bigmattystyles
comments.story: Intruder at the top of the 20 meter amateur band?
comments.text: Do exchanges like HF traders? I know HF traders themselves justify their own existence by claiming they provide liquidity to the markets, but I've always just sort-of rolled my eyes at that. They only extract value and provide none, in my opinion, tax the profits heavily. I think every exchange should pad each order by a random number between 0 and 250ms, it would take care of it.
